Rotate into IDX tech proxies (NINE) for domestic AI adoption. Trim after +10% single-day spikes; hold core through Q3 earnings catalysts.

Position for Q3 loan-growth acceleration and fee-income recovery, favoring niche lenders over big banks.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Indonesia's coal export competitiveness is structurally underpinned by domestic market obligations (DMO) and low-cost strip-mining, insulating margins even if seaborne thermal prices soften.
Gold miners (MDKA, SMMT) benefit from a durable central-bank buying cycle and rupiah depreciation, which amplifies local-currency revenue from USD-priced bullion.
Copper's supply deficit, driven by smelter bottlenecks in China and declining ore grades globally, supports FCX and Indonesian copper-gold developers as long-term re-rating catalysts.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in coal and gold names (GTBO, ALKA, MBMA, MDKA) as the IDX energy complex re-rates on resilient thermal demand and rupiah tailwinds; FCX's copper strength confirms global metal bid. Rotate out of laggards into high-beta winners within 48 hours, targeting +5-8% before signal fades.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US solar and storage names benefit from a durable AI/data-center electricity demand supercycle, lifting volumes and pricing power beyond policy cycles.
Indonesia's renewables upside hinges on geothermal and transmission infrastructure, where PLN's capex and regulatory reform, not solar module costs, drive structural growth.
Climate-tech capital is rotating toward profitable scale-ups (FSLR, ENPH) over speculative hydrogen (PLUG), signaling a quality-over-growth regime that favors cash-generative US names.
sectors.ai: Buy the US-listed solar/energy-storage complex on the AI-driven power-demand narrative; SEDG, ENPH, and FSLR lead with margin recovery and US policy tailwinds. In Indonesia, stay selective—domestic renewables lag, so focus on geothermal and grid capex names tied to PLN's 2030 targets, not solar. Overweight US names, underweight ID pure-plays until tariff clarity and project awards firm.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Indonesia's FMCG sector is structurally supported by a rising middle class and urbanization, which sustains volume growth for local brands even as global peers decelerate.
Regulatory tailwinds on domestic content requirements and food security push manufacturers to localize supply chains, boosting margins for agile mid-caps over import-dependent multinationals.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are compressing go-to-market costs, enabling smaller listed players to scale faster and re-rate, as seen in today's 10-20% single-day moves.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian consumer names on momentum, but rotate out of crowded staples into mid-cap turnaround stories (PPRI, MSJA, JAWA) where local demand and margin repair are driving outsized gains; the US drag is noise—IDX consumer leadership confirms domestic resilience, so add on any pullback toward 5%+ upside names with clean balance sheets.
